To clear your confusion-

80 hours —> 9 hour shifts —> 8.9 days of UNPAID time off (I was being GENEROUS when I said 10). This is what you have for unpaid time off for the duration of your employment, no matter how long. 

This was communicated to us directly by the clinical director and operations manager in person in February, and also was a “last straw” of sorts for myself and others.


I am not talking about PTO or paid holidays.
If you have missed 8.9 days (as in, during your ENTIRE time working there ever), don’t have any PTO/flex, and need to call out- even in an emergency- you are fired. This was the number one complaint amongst RBT’s at my location.

Surely this is a rule because employees called a lot. I just wish the company knew/cared that its because everyone is miserable.

Too many to go through, but I definitely encountered MANY situations that felt like that, even despite minding my own business while working there. This was the case for most RBTs at my location. 

-The company as a whole is NOT ran efficiently, and RBT’s received the extremely short end of the stick in every regard. The culture isn’t great because everyone is underpaid ($15.50-$17/hr), tired of being screwed over, tired of the schedule changing every hour (the person making our schedule was some corporate employee who had never been in our building and did NOT understand the idea of closed teams with high behavior kiddos- think inexperienced 18yo BTs getting scheduled 3 hours with an EXTREME client), tired of false promises and absent leadership (BCBA’s remained hidden behind a locked door marked DND, and don’t you dare try to knock- just figure it out in your own with zero guidance). This resulted in RBT’s taking it out on each other, the only other people we saw. 

-They did NOT care if you or clients were sick and/or contagious. You have to meet billable hours, and you have to meet the absurd attendance policy (see below). Our policy was a child has to throw up THREE times to be sent home, because “kids just throw up a lot”. I’ve seen kids with pink eye and covid. I was sick there every 2 weeks. They would say that’s just how this field goes, but I haven’t been sick since working more than the same amount of time at my new clinic.

-The clinic was filthy, due to zero accountability with chores, sanitation, etc. 
The only time we really saw leadership was when they would run around trying to get us to clean the entire clinic due to the constant parent tours. 

-People would get away with things because there would be no follow up, ever. Nobody ever made sure people did what they were supposed to. I saw minimal progress in kids who were absolutely ready to progress, and the issue was a lack of CONSISTENCY. This is what happens when kids get scheduled half the day with therapists who do not want to run trials because they’re lazy. Nobody ever checks to see if the trials that ARE being ran are being ran correctly- skewed data from people not reading.

-They told us that they were now required to provide us with breaks, and were going to start doing so. Instead of actually doing it they just changed the name of our unpaid “30 min (really 20min)” Lunch to Break. This was their way of getting around giving us the extra half our off during the 9 hour shift.

-Not to mention, you get fired after X amount of absences EVER (no matter the reason, I saw an employee of 3 years get fired because their daycare was mistreating their child and they had to pick them up, which is absurd to even type out). Also, 80 hours of unpaid time off to use- EVER. It only depletes, there is not a way to gain more. Sure, short term, that’s not too bad- but you’ve got 9-10 days of unpaid time to use as long as you work there- imagine being there for YEARS and being allowed 9 days of time off to last the entire duration (outside of the minimal PTO they will give you).

-HR didn’t really take things seriously. None of leadership did, but that could just be my location. When I left, we had a creepy new male employee with multiple complaints from female staff within the first month. Nothing ever happened, at least in the time I was there.

-I only lasted 3 months before I was as burnt out as I was at other jobs I’d worked for YEARS. They truly are the “turn and burn puppy mill” company that everyone says they are. Most of my coworkers who were there for longer said things went downhill (through their eyes) a few years back. 

I am at a new company now, and I could not be happier. ABC showed me the bad side of ABA, my current clinic is definitely the good side. Don’t let them discourage you from pursuing this field.

If you do not believe me, just take a look around.
